title: High Speed Rail Planning Authority Bill 2013
short_title: High Speed Rail Planning Authority Bill 2013

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would establish a planning authority to advise on and develop high speed rail along Australia’s east coast and arrange reservation of its corridor.
The authority would have eleven members drawn from ministerial appointments, state and territory nominees, local government and the rail industry, serving three-year appointment terms.
It would begin operating under the Act when a budget appropriation was made for the authority, and report annually to the Minister for presentation to Parliament.
changes: The authority would receive powers to carry out land use planning and consult the public.
Staff and consultants could be engaged to support its work.
The Minister could require reports or information about matters within the authority’s functions.
summary.affected: The authority, participating governments, local government and rail industry bodies, and members of the public consulted on high speed rail are affected.

speeches.speaker: Anthony Albanese
speeches.brief: Argued for the High Speed Rail Planning Authority Bill 2013, citing a feasibility study finding the Brisbane to Melbourne line would cost $114 billion, and criticised the government for cutting the $52 million allocated to begin planning for the project, including securing the rail corridor.
